title: Perfection of a pseudo-coherent complex can be checked on localizations at primes or at maximal ideals
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma lists five conditions on a pseudo-coherent complex K^bullet over a ring R: that it be perfect; that its localization at every prime be perfect; the same at every maximal ideal; the vanishing of H^i(K^bullet tensor^L kappa(p)) for all i much smaller than 0 at every prime; and the same at every maximal ideal; it asserts the implications (1) => (2) <=> (3) <=> (4) <=> (5), with all conditions equivalent when K^bullet is bounded below (source lines 20063-20086). The proof has real content beyond the formal implications. The localization implications come from applying the pullback-perfect lemma to the appropriate maps of local rings and residue fields, and the passage from primes to maximal ideals uses that every prime lies in a maximal ideal and then pulls back along R_m -> R_p (proof lines 20089-20097). The substantive direction is that (4) implies (2) and (5) implies (3): in the local case with vanishing below degree a, the proof invokes the cutting lemma at i = a - 1 to split K^bullet as the direct sum of tau_{<= a-1} and tau_{>= a} with the upper part perfect, and then shows the lower part vanishes by a contradiction: if not, the largest nonzero cohomology module M is finite by pseudo-coherence, so by Nakayama M tensor_R kappa is nonzero, which makes H^i((tau_{<= a-1}K^bullet) tensor^L kappa) = H^i(K^bullet tensor^L kappa) nonzero, contradicting the hypothesis (proof lines 20100-20122). The bounded below case is then finished by producing, at any given maximal ideal, an f outside it with K^bullet tensor R_f perfect, using the gluing and lift lemmas together with quasi-compactness (proof lines 20125-20132). The non-routine steps are the Nakayama contradiction and the final local-to-global promotion.
